event.title: Highest temperature in Munich on July 30?

eventMetadata.context_description: Forecast models from NOAA and the National Weather Service show the highest uncertainty for New York City’s July 30 high temperature centered on the 76–81°F range, with market-implied probabilities reflecting modest differences in expected afternoon heating. Key drivers include the strength of an approaching weak surface high, boundary-layer moisture levels, and the timing of any thin mid-level cloud deck that could limit insolation. Ensemble spreads in the GFS and ECMWF runs highlight small variations in 850-hPa temperatures and dew points that translate directly into one- to two-degree differences at Central Park’s official observing site. With the urban heat island effect adding roughly 2–4°F above surrounding rural readings under light winds, traders are weighting the latest 12z model guidance and any overnight sounding updates that could shift the most likely bin before markets close.
